committed_before_any_measurement: These rules are in the commit before spikes/m6_f5_sensors.py first runs on either machine. They do not change after a result. A fix to a program bug is allowed, and each attempt is recorded.
question: Does the camera sensor of cumlx.render give on Metal what it gives on CUDA, for RGB, depth and segmentation together? This is F5 at its target grade B.
versions: The V100 runs Mitsuba 3.8.0 cuda_ad_rgb and the Mac 3.9.1 metal_ad_rgb: Mitsuba 3.9 refuses a GPU under compute capability 7.5 and 3.8.0 has no Metal variant, as in validation/m5-render.json. So the comparison covers a version difference too
scenes: spikes/m6_f5_sensors.py: box_scene of cumlx.render.sensors (a cube over a floor under a constant light), the cube at three poses, seen by two cameras: six views at 256 x 256

rgb.what: Sensors.rgb at 1024 samples per pixel, seeds 1, 2, 3 on CUDA and 11, 12, 13 on the Mac, each view compared by cumlx.render.compare.compare_images
rgb.source: The M5 rule of validation/m5-render-limits.json: PSNR floor 40 dB, MSE across devices at most twice the MSE within a device, channel means within max(3 standard errors, 1%)

depth_and_segmentation.what: Sensors.depth_segmentation with one sample at each pixel centre (a stratified sampler without jitter), against the exact depth and label of the pixel-centre ray in float64, on each machine, and between the machines
depth_and_segmentation.measure: depth: the largest absolute difference over the pixels where both sides hit the same shape. label: the fraction of pixels whose shape differs, a miss counted as a shape
depth_and_segmentation.source: The limits of validation/m5-lidar-limits.json: 1 mm for a float32 ray, and one ray in a thousand for the edges of shapes

controls.what: the Mac side with spikes/m6_f5_sensors.py --fault: each must fail on at least one view
controls.box_5cm: the cube drawn 5 cm off its pose: depth and segmentation against the exact values
controls.light_2pct: the light 2% stronger: RGB against CUDA. The same fault failed against CUDA in validation/m5-render.json

grade: B when every part passes on the first complete run of both machines
not_a_pass: A part with no output, a missing variant, a stop for memory, disk or time, and a run that started while the GPU was busy.
